# requires: wire
#
# A Last-Modified in the obsolete RFC 850 spelling, which RFC 9110 requires a
# recipient to accept and forbids a sender to use. Servers send it anyway.
#
# The value is never interpreted -- it is echoed back verbatim as If-Range, and
# the origin server evaluates that by exact match -- so accepting it is a
# question about which spellings are recognised and not about parsing a date.
# Until 2026-09-06 the three implementations answered it three ways, because
# each asked its own standard library instead of the contract: Go took a
# three-letter timezone the grammar does not allow, Python took RFC 2822, and
# C++ dropped everything but IMF-fixdate. A dropped validator is a resume that
# cannot name its version, and no other line in a transcript shows it.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=http:obsoletedate
run A alpha
state A

# expect 2: ok state=transferred
# expect 2: done=64 err=none
# expect 2: cp={"verified_prefix":64,"validators":{"last_modified":"Sunday, 06-Nov-94 08:49:37 GMT"}} [DL-V5]
